title: Software Development Engineer II (Frontend) - Opportunities
description:
About HighLevel:

HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes.

To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value, demonstrating the impact of shared infrastructure at scale. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently.

Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability.

Our people

With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Our impact

Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that.

Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts

About the Role:

We are looking for an SDE-2 Frontend-leaning Full-Stack Engineer to build the interface of CRM Opportunities, the deal and pipeline engine at the heart of our CRM. Opportunities is the system of record for every revenue motion our customers run, from lead conversion to closed-won, and the pipeline board is where our customers spend their working day.

This role is frontend-first. The hard problems here are interface problems: a drag-and-drop pipeline board that stays smooth with thousands of cards on screen, optimistic updates that roll back cleanly when a write fails, deal detail views assembled from arbitrary customer-defined custom fields, filters and saved views that hold up under real use, and keeping all of it coherent as several people move deals in the same pipeline at once. Getting this right is the difference between a CRM customers tolerate and one they trust.

You will own frontend features end-to-end in Vue.js, and you will go into the backend as the work requires — extending an API, shaping a response so the client does not have to over-fetch, adding an endpoint that serves the view you are building. You do not need to be a backend specialist; you do need to be unafraid of the server side and happy to work in it rather than filing a ticket. Senior engineers own the broader architecture and are there for design guidance and review.

What You Will Do:

- Own frontend features across Opportunities in Vue.js — the pipeline board, deal detail views, stage and pipeline configuration, filters and saved views, bulk actions, and reporting surfaces 
- Build interactions that have to feel instant: drag-and-drop stage moves, inline edits, optimistic updates with clean rollback and clear error states when a write fails 
- Make large pipelines fast in the browser — virtualized and windowed lists, pagination and lazy loading, render and re-render cost, bundle size, and time to first meaningful paint on a board with thousands of deals 
- Design and maintain client-side state and data-fetching patterns (Pinia/Vuex, caching, invalidation) so the UI stays consistent without redundant round-trips 
- Handle concurrency in the interface: live updates when a teammate moves a deal, stale-data detection, and sensible conflict resolution 
- Render dynamic, customer-defined schemas — custom fields, custom objects, and per-workspace configuration — without special-casing every variation 
- Build reusable, well-composed components, and contribute to the shared design system rather than growing one-off UI 
- Work directly from designs, and push back with product and design where an interaction will not hold up in practice 
- Extend the backend where your feature needs it: adding or reshaping NestJS API endpoints, trimming over-fetching, and adjusting payloads for the view you are building 
- Write tests that matter — component and unit tests, plus end-to-end coverage of the flows customers cannot afford to have broken 
- Instrument the frontend: error tracking, real-user performance monitoring, and the event data needed to see how a feature is actually used 
- Care about accessibility, keyboard support, responsive layout, and cross-browser behavior as part of shipping, not as a follow-up 
- Take part in on-call for the surfaces you own, debug production issues, and contribute to postmortems 
- Write clear design docs for the features you own, and participate actively in design and code review 

What You will Need:

- 3+ years building and shipping production frontend applications 
- Strong JavaScript/TypeScript fundamentals, and depth in a component framework — Vue preferred, React fine if you are willing to work in Vue 
- Real experience with complex, stateful interfaces — not just forms and CRUD screens 
- Practical grasp of frontend performance: rendering cost, long lists, network waterfalls, bundle size, and how to profile rather than guess 
- Comfortable consuming and debugging REST APIs, and confident enough in a backend codebase (Node.js/NestJS or similar) to make the change your feature needs 
- Solid CSS and layout skills, and an eye for whether a build matches the design 
- Experience shipping and supporting features you wrote — design through deploy 
- Comfort working with a degree of ambiguity, asking good questions, and driving a task to done 

Preferred Qualifications:

- Built a board, kanban, table, grid, or calendar interface with drag-and-drop and large data volumes 
- Exposure to CRM, sales, pipeline, or workflow products 
- Experience with dynamic or schema-driven UI — rendering interfaces from customer-defined configuration 
- Worked on real-time or collaborative interfaces (WebSockets, polling, optimistic concurrency) 
- Experience with multi-tenant SaaS, including white-labelled or themeable products 
- Familiarity with Vue 3, Pinia, Vite, and end-to-end testing (Playwright or Cypress) 
- Backend experience with Node.js/NestJS and MongoDB 
- Product instincts and a portfolio or GitHub of shipped work — we will want to look at interfaces you have built 

Tech Skill Set:

Vue.js (Vue 3, Pinia, Vite), TypeScript, modern CSS — backed by Node.js (NestJS) APIs, MongoDB, and Redis, running on a distributed microservices architecture over Istio service mesh.

What Success Looks Like:

- Ships Opportunities frontend features to production reliably, with steadily less guidance over time 
- Builds interfaces that stay fast and predictable as workspaces grow from hundreds to millions of deals 
- Turns fiddly interaction problems into implementations that hold up in real customer use, not just in a demo 
- Leaves the component layer better composed and more reusable than they found it 
- Makes the backend change their feature needs instead of waiting on someone else 
- Debugs production issues independently and leaves behind better instrumentation than they found 
- Grows into owning larger, more ambiguous pieces of the product

While prior experience with XMPRO is not required, familiarity with similar tools like Grafana or Tableau is valuable.

Why join Weir?

We live our values we think safety first, do the right thing, respect each other, aim high, and delight our customers. We encourage our people to lead by example and celebrate our successes.

We’re passionate about our purpose to help deliver the natural resources that are essential to create a better future for the world. We do this by combining our deep customer insights, world-class engineering, materials science expertise, and intelligent automation to deliver innovative end-to-end solutions incorporating our signature technologies.

We believe your voice matters and your ideas make a difference. We’re working hard to nurture a diverse culture where our people feel like they belong and can do the best work of their lives. You can help shape our unique culture through our inclusion networks and safety initiatives.

The Software Engineer-II for Ads builds the data, analytics, and product experiences that help Merchants and Brands understand advertising performance and decide where to invest next. This role will strengthen the Ads experience across the customer-facing Brand Experience platform and the internal Merchant Station platform by turning complex advertising data and business logic into clear, actionable insights.

Ads, together with DART and margin calculators, is a critical input into day-to-day Merchant decisions. The current Ads experience is one of the least-used areas in Brand Experience because it does not yet provide essential data, including keyword-level detail, or a compelling explanation of performance. This engineer will help overhaul that experience, support rapid proofs of concept, and build scalable capabilities that contribute to Merchandising's goal in additional programmatic Brand support across Ads, Promotions, and Pricing Support.

What Success Looks Like
• Delivers a significantly improved Ads experience in Brand Experience and Merchant Station, increasing engagement with a page that currently has the lowest usage on the platform.

• Provides Merchants and Brands with accurate, decision-ready advertising data, including keyword-level performance insights.

• Enables Merchants to audit advertising spend, explain the impact of Project Astra, and present a clear story about Spreetail's advertising strategy and results.

• Builds actionable recommendations that help Brands understand when and where additional advertising investment can create value.

• Runs focused proofs of concept quickly, incorporates feedback, and scales successful approaches into reliable product capabilities.

• Contributes to Merchandising's goal of securing $1 million in additional programmatic Brand support across Ads, Promotions, and Pricing Support.

• Improves the reliability, clarity, and usability of advertising data across both internal and Brand-facing workflows.

Key Responsibilities
Design, build, test, and maintain full-stack features for Ads across Brand Experience and Merchant Station.

• Develop data services and visualizations that show advertising performance, spend, impact, and opportunities for action.

• Translate advertising strategy, Project Astra outputs, and complex business rules into clear product experiences for Merchants and Brands.

• Create keyword-level and other detailed views needed to diagnose performance and support investment decisions.

• Integrate advertising data into existing Merch Tech workflows while maintaining accuracy, freshness, and consistency.

• Partner with Merchants, Product, Design, Data, and engineering teammates to clarify user needs and prioritize the highest-value capabilities.

• Develop proofs of concept to test how Ads insights and storytelling can increase Brand engagement and support dollars.

• Improve deployment workflows so new data, metrics, and product enhancements can reach users faster and more safely.

• Apply strong engineering practices, including code reviews, automated testing, monitoring, documentation, and maintainable system design.

• Investigate production issues, resolve data or experience gaps, and continuously improve platform performance and usability.

Key Metrics You Will Impact 
• Engagement and adoption of Ads capabilities in Brand Experience and Merchant Station.

• Availability and completeness of decision-critical Ads data, including keyword-level information.

• Merchant ability to audit advertising spend and communicate advertising performance to Brands.

• Speed and quality of proofs of concept, experiments, and subsequent production releases.

• Contribution toward $1 million in additional programmatic Brand support across Ads, Promotions, and Pricing Support.

• Data accuracy, platform reliability, defect rates, and time to resolve issues.

• Cycle time for introducing new Ads data, insights, and user actions into the platforms.

Skills and Experience 

• Strong 3-5 years of full-stack development skills, with experience connecting backend data services to intuitive front-end experiences.

• Experience developing analytics, reporting, or data-visualization products that help users make decisions.

• Ability to translate complex business logic and large datasets into accurate, understandable, and actionable product features.

• Experience working with APIs, data integrations, data quality checks, and modern software delivery practices.

title: Full Stack Developer - Cloud & Security
description:
Our electric vehicles stream telemetry to the cloud, where it powers a dashboard, engineering analytics, and remote operations. We are looking for a Full Stack Developer who can build across the whole stack - front-end dashboards, back-end services, and the cloud architecture that connects our vehicles to the cloud - with a strong, security-first mindset for a connected-vehicle product.
You will own significant parts of the telemetry and dashboard platform end to end, and help ensure the device-to-cloud pipeline is scalable, observable, and secure. We care about strong engineering fundamentals and the ability to pick the right tool for the problem - specific languages, frameworks, and cloud providers are secondary to solid architecture and delivery.

Key Responsibilities
- Build and maintain the fleet/telemetry dashboard(modern front-end framework) and back-end services / APIs, including real-time data streaming.
- Design and evolve the cloud architecture— compute, storage, managed messaging/IoT, and time-series data — on a major cloud platform.
- Own the device-to-cloud data pipeline — telemetry ingestion (e.g. MQTT or equivalent), processing, and time-series storage.
- Apply security across the stack: secure coding (OWASP Top 10), device authentication with certificates and mutual TLS, PKI/certificate lifecycle, authentication/authorization, and secrets management.
- Define and provision infrastructure as code and maintain CI/CD pipelines.
- Own test automation — unit, integration, and end-to-end tests — and build quality into the delivery pipeline.
- Set up monitoring, logging, and observability for the platform.
- Collaborate with the firmware team on device connectivity, provisioning, and secure OTA.

Outcomes You Own
- Deliver reliable, real-time telemetry from device to dashboard at fleet scale.
- Harden the device-to-cloud path (certificates, authorization, secrets) with no critical security gaps.
- Codify infrastructure and CI/CD so the platform is reproducible and observable.

Required Qualifications
- B.E./B.Tech/M.C.A. in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
- 3–6 years building full-stack web applications, with strong command of at least one modern front-end framework and one back-end language/runtime.
- Solid database fundamentals — relational schema design, plus comfort with the data model that fits the workload (relational, time-series, document, etc.).
- Hands-on experience architecting and operating on a major cloud platform (any of AWS, Azure, or GCP), including infrastructure-as-code.
- Working knowledge of application & cloud security: OWASP Top 10, TLS/PKI, authentication/authorization, and secrets handling.
- Version control, CI/CD, and automated-testing discipline.
﻿
Preferred / Nice-to-Have
- IoT experience — device-to-cloud messaging, managed IoT services, and device certificate/fleet provisioning.
- Handling time-series / high-volume telemetry data at scale, and building operational dashboards.
- Containerization and orchestration.
- Familiarity with modern end-to-end and unit test frameworks.
- Security depth — threat modeling, pen-test familiarity, or a recognized security certification.
- Exposure to connected-vehicle / automotive cybersecurity concepts (e.g. ISO/SAE 21434).

=================

We are looking for a **Senior Software Engineer – AI & Agentic Engineering** to build and deliver AI-enabled solutions that change how business and technology teams plan, build, and make decisions. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who combines solid full-stack skills—**a strong UI framework, backend services, and Python**—with practical experience applying **Generative AI and agentic patterns**.

The role is not tied to a single line of business (LOB). You will work across **multiple LOBs in an Agile setup**, partnering closely with business stakeholders, product owners, and fellow engineers to turn business needs into secure, observable, and measurable AI capabilities. **Hands-on experience building AI and Agentic AI solutions is mandatory and can come from any technology stack**. Experience with **Google Cloud Platform (GCP)** and **Google’s Agent Development Kit (ADK)** is good to have. You will also instrument solutions with **OpenTelemetry** and build the **metrics** that show business value.

  
  

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

**1. AI & Agentic Solution Engineering**
----------------------------------------

* Design and build AI agents and multi-agent workflows using modern agentic frameworks (e.g., Google ADK, LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, CrewAI, or similar) and leading LLMs.

* Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool and function calling, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, and agent-to-agent patterns that connect AI to enterprise data and systems.

* Build and maintain evaluation tests for AI quality, including accuracy, groundedness, hallucination, and guardrail checks, to support release-readiness decisions.

* Apply responsible AI practices, including guardrails, prompt and context engineering, data privacy, and human-in-the-loop controls.

* Help optimize AI solutions for cost, latency, and scalability, including model selection, token usage, and caching.

----------------------------------------------------

**3. Observability, Telemetry & Metrics**

* Define and build metrics that connect technical performance to business outcomes, such as adoption, cycle-time reduction, AI quality, cost per transaction, and productivity gains.

* Build dashboards and alerts (e.g., Grafana, Google Cloud Monitoring, or equivalent) that give engineering, product, and leadership teams clear visibility.

* Contribute to SLIs and SLOs for AI-enabled services, and use data to improve reliability, cost, and quality.

**4. Business Partnership Across LOBs**
---------------------------------------

* Work closely with business stakeholders and product owners across multiple LOBs to understand workflows, pain points, and opportunities where AI can create measurable value.

* Translate business needs into technical designs, user stories, and acceptance criteria in an Agile (Scrum/SAFe) delivery model.

* Run demos, pilots, and feedback loops with business users to validate value and drive adoption.

* Explain complex AI concepts, trade-offs, and results in clear, business-friendly language.

* Follow and contribute to engineering standards for AI development, evaluation, observability, security, and code quality.

* Take part in design and code reviews, and share knowledge to raise the team’s AI fluency.

**Technologies**

title: Senior Software Engineer - Data Warehousing & Transformation Ecosystem
location: New York, Philadelphia, Chicago, Boston, United States (remote)
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Connectors team is the bridge between ClickHouse and the broader data ecosystem. We build and maintain the integrations that make ClickHouse accessible to millions of developers, data practitioners and AI agents worldwide: data visualization plugins (Tableau, Power BI, Superset, Metabase), connectors for data frameworks (Apache Spark, Flink, Kafka Connect, Beam, Fivetran), transformation and orchestration tooling (dbt, Airflow, Dagster), and AI tooling.

Our work directly shapes how companies process massive datasets: real-time analytics platforms ingesting millions of events per second, observability systems monitoring global infrastructure, and the data warehouses and AI-powered applications redefining how teams work with data. We collaborate closely with the open-source community, internal teams, and enterprise users to ensure ClickHouse integrations set the standard for performance, reliability, and developer experience.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Software Engineer focused on the data warehousing ecosystem, you will own how ClickHouse plugs into the modern analytics-engineering toolchain. This role sits at the intersection of high-performance database engineering, developer experience, and production operations. You will build the integrations that let data teams use ClickHouse as the warehouse behind the tools they already run, and you will own how those integrations are deployed and operated at scale.

You will drive architecture, performance, and feature direction across four areas:

 - Transformation: dbt, across both the Python-based v1 adapter and the Rust-based v2 (Fusion) engine; SQLMesh

 - Semantic layer: dbt Semantic Layer / MetricFlow, Cube, Apache Ossie (formerly Open Semantic Interchange)

 - Schema and metadata management: schema evolution, model contracts, migration tooling, catalog integration

 - Orchestration: Apache Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, Temporal, and how transformation jobs run inside them (Astronomer Cosmos, dagster-dbt)

We are looking for someone who has run the transformation layer of a real data warehouse, not just written models in it. You have operated dbt and its orchestration for many teams: CI/CD, environments, scheduling, credentials, observability, and cost. You know what breaks at scale because you were the one paged for it. You know what it takes to maintain code that other teams’ pipelines depend on – ideally because you’ve contributed to the open-source data warehousing ecosystem yourself (dbt and its adapters, orchestration providers, semantic-layer tooling or similar). You bring that practitioner's insight into what we should build and why, and you turn it into robust, production-ready integrations and the deployment artifacts (container images, Helm charts, reference architectures) that make ClickHouse the natural choice when data teams design their next warehouse.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own and evolve dbt-clickhouse and related transformation adapters to enterprise-grade quality: correctness, performance, and reliability across dbt versions and engines

 - Design and build ClickHouse integrations for semantic-layer tooling (MetricFlow, Cube, Apache Ossie), making ClickHouse a first-class target for governed metrics consumed by BI tools and AI agents

 - Build and maintain orchestration integrations (Airflow provider, Dagster, Prefect) and the patterns for running transformation jobs inside them

 - Define how schema evolution, model contracts, and migrations work across the toolchain when ClickHouse is the warehouse

 - Own the production deployment and operations story for these integrations: container images, Helm charts, reference architectures, and runbooks for running transformation and orchestration workloads on Kubernetes against ClickHouse

 - Build and operate the Kubernetes-based CI, integration-test, and benchmark infrastructure

 - Engage actively with the open-source community: triage issues, support contributors, advocate for users, and shape the roadmap from real-world feedback

 - Collaborate with Product, Cloud, and core database teams to align integration work with broader priorities

 - Bring a practitioner's perspective to roadmap decisions, grounding prioritization in how data and analytics engineers actually operate a warehouse


ABOUT YOU

 - 7+ years of software development experience, including hands-on time as a Data Engineer, Analytics Engineer, or Data Platform Engineer

 - Deep dbt experience from both sides: you have run large dbt projects in production, and you understand how an adapter plugs into dbt-core

 - You have built or operated an internal data platform that served multiple teams: CI/CD for transformation projects, orchestration, environment promotion, secrets and credentials, observability, and cost attribution

 - You have run dbt and an orchestrator (Airflow, Dagster or Temporal) in production on Kubernetes, and you’ve owned the deployment and reliability of both — not just the models.

 - Strong database fundamentals: SQL, data modeling, query optimization, and familiarity with OLAP or columnar databases

 - Outstanding written and verbal communication; comfortable collaborating across engineering functions and with open-source communities


BONUS POINTS

 - Proven contributions to the open-source data warehousing ecosystem

 - Familiarity with ClickHouse or similar high-performance OLAP databases; MergeTree internals a plus

 - Hands-on experience with semantic-layer tooling (MetricFlow, Cube, Apache Ossie, AtScale) or BI semantic models

 - Experience exposing governed data to AI tooling: MCP servers, text-to-SQL grounding, agent-facing data APIs

 - Familiarity with Rust & the Data Fusion ecosystem

 - Familiarity with the JVM ecosystem


PERKS

 - Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

 - Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

 - Equity in the company - Every new eligible team member who joins our company receives equity.

 - Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

 - A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

 - Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.
